question: A 35-year-old patient presents with new-onset hyperglycaemia, weight loss, and polyuria over 4 weeks. HbA1c is 11.2%. He has no family history of T2DM. Which feature most strongly supports a diagnosis of Type 1 rather than Type 2 diabetes?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: An HbA1c of 11.2% indicates poor glycaemic control but is not specific to either T1DM or T2DM.
While T1DM classically presents in youth, late-onset T1DM (LADA) can present in adults up to age 50. Age alone is insufficient.

answers.text: Rapid onset with significant weight loss and absence of metabolic syndrome features

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Abrupt onset, weight loss (catabolism from insulin deficiency), absence of obesity/metabolic syndrome, and no family history of T2DM all favour T1DM or LADA; C-peptide and anti-GAD antibodies would confirm.
Polyuria and polydipsia are non-specific symptoms of any type of hyperglycaemia and do not help differentiate T1DM from T2DM.

overallFeedback.feedback: Differentiating T1DM from T2DM requires a clinical pattern: T1DM typically has rapid onset, weight loss, ketosis-prone, no metabolic syndrome, and positive autoantibodies (anti-GAD, anti-IA2).
Correct — acute onset with weight loss and lack of insulin resistance features favours autoimmune (T1DM/LADA). Confirm with C-peptide and anti-GAD antibodies.
